## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded by [source-2@L1382-L1401|claim=formal-document]. For \(a=1,b=2\), the stated interval consists exactly of \(x_0,x_1,x_2\).
- claim-2: The strategy proves the claim under the recorded hypotheses. Source-backed ideal generation yields the graded surjection because \(A/A_+\cong\mathbb Z\). Its domain is supported only in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\); the accepted boundary certificates cover all cases with \(\min(q-i,r-j)=1\) and show the corresponding component maps are isomorphisms. Thus the homogeneous kernel vanishes degreewise and hence globally. The conclusion is limited correctly to \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\), without asserting minimality or a broader theorem.

## Required revisions
- None. The requested standalone globalization certificate is established conditionally on the recorded integral presentation hypotheses and accepted degreewise certificates.
